claim: two admitted tt-npe twin cores agree exactly with tt-npe's own code over balanced random inputs
scope: 2 of the 3 directly-callable cores. interpolateBW (rate_resolution_pkg) NOT yet done.

oracle.host: gertrude (x86_64) — tt-npe 6967ce36 built from source with g++ 13.3
oracle.calls: THEIR npeTransferDependencyTracker, THEIR Grid2D<int>, THEIR MulticastCoordSet::grid_size()
oracle.note: no arithmetic re-implemented in the harness; the flat cell index is read out of their own operator() by address arithmetic

twin.harness: hand-written, pragma SPARK_Mode (Off), instrumentation only, never admitted

coverage.note: first run was skewed (58/400 in-bounds, 60/400 done) and was rerun with rebalanced inputs

mutation_check.why: a differential reporting 0 mismatches is worthless unless it can report non-zero

what_this_does_NOT_establish: transfer_progress_pkg and timestep_pkg — their expressions live inside the loop body and are not callable; testing them would compare the twin against a transcription, not against their code
rate_resolution_pkg — interpolateBW is callable but not yet driven; float-vs-integer needs a stated tolerance
agreement on inputs outside the sampled ranges
anything about tt-npe's correctness; this is agreement, not correctness
